translation_notes: The one-step for-loop (g.objects(coded_entry, FHIR.CodeableConcept.coding)) becomes for codeable_concept in m{ {coded_entry} fhir:CodeableConcept.coding ?o } — arity 1, terms not one-tuples, exactly the target of this stratum.

Also translated the two g.value(..., any=False) traversals (coded_entry, and the coding's rdf:type) to m{ }.first() (trav_single_value idiom, same region): most-specific construction per INSTRUCTIONS_403 §2, not left as raw rdflib calls.

any=False adds a uniqueness check (raises if >1 match) that .first() does not reproduce (.first() silently takes the first). The fixture keeps both call sites to at most one match, so this gap is not exercised here; flagged since it is a real, if narrow, semantic gap between g.value(any=False) and .first().

FHIR's dotted RDF vocabulary (fhir:Coding.system, fhir:CodeableConcept.coding) needs a literal interior dot in the prefixed name's local part. Confirms lexical.md: interior dots are accepted inside islands (m{ }) via Turtle's full PN_CHARS rules. Outside an island the same name would NOT parse this way (dot ends a Python identifier there), which is why value(g, codeable_concept, FHIR.Coding.system) keeps FHIR.Coding.system as plain Python (it addresses the project's own value() helper, not an rdflib traversal) rather than becoming fhir:Coding.system.

The source repository (BD2KOnFHIR/fhirtordf) is unavailable to this venv: it pins rdflib~=5.0, incompatible with this study's rdflib 7.2.1. Added fhirgraphutils_context.py, a context shim reproducing (from the published 1.3.3 source) the DottedNamespace/DottedURIRef pair that makes FHIR.Coding.system work, plus the value() helper and CodeableConcept class the extracted region calls but does not define; both original.py and translated.ldpy import the same shim.
predicate: URIRef is a parameter, not a constant vocabulary term, so it is interpolated ({predicate}) rather than written as a prefixed name — same treatment as {subject}.

Repair 2026-11-02 (hollow green): the original returned [] on every call because the context shim's DottedURIRef lacked the repository's `__eq__`/`__hash__` (and DottedNamespace's `__getattribute__`/`__eq__`/`__hash__`), so under rdflib 7.2.1 `g.objects(s, FHIR.CodeableConcept.coding)` never matched the stored URIRef. The shim now carries the repository's overrides (dottednamespace.py at 05b23ba); the original then returns the codings. The driver gains five calls (other system, unmatched system, neighbouring subject, other predicate, a subject with incomplete codings) and the fixture a patient3. Translation unchanged; mutants (wrong coding predicate, subject ignored, join widened, `coding_code` guard dropped) each FAIL; hollow_green.py no longer lists the pair.

2026-11-03: FHIR dotted local names written with Turtle's escape, `fhir:X\.y` (and `fhir:X\/n`), which ldpy reads outside islands since c0e1ca6; they replace full IRIs or `FHIR.X.y` attribute chains that the earlier limit forced (record ldpy/012). Five check lines OK.

repair.driver: eight calls instead of three (other system, unmatched system, neighbouring subject, other predicate, incomplete codings) and patient3 added to fixture.ttl; the shim fhirgraphutils_context.py now carries the repository's DottedURIRef/DottedNamespace __eq__, __hash__ and __getattribute__, without which the original returned [] everywhere.
repair.remaining: The shim was edited (a transcription fidelity fix, not an invented input type); previous notes saying 'unmodified' described the first transcription.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the `list(...)` around g.objects() goes (the loop does not modify the graph). Nothing else compresses: the `if coded_entry:` guard must stay (g.objects(None, P) would be a wildcard), the filter needs both values twice so a comprehension would need a walrus, and both `g.value(..., any=False)` stay.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the coding loop iterates `m{ {coded_entry} fhir:CodeableConcept.coding ?o }(g)` (182 tokens, as with `@graph g`; 185 with the Python selector) and `RDF.type` becomes `rdf:type`. Unlike translated.ldpy, both `g.value(..., any=False)` reads stay Python: `.first()` drops the UniquenessError they raise on two values, and `.one()` also raises on zero, where value() returns None. `FHIR.Coding.system`/`.code` stay, passed to the project's value() helper. The ldpy artefact is longer than optimized.py (ratio 1.028): the two `@prefix` lines of the header outweigh what the island saves.

optimized_header.ldpy: the same names go, and RDF too (replaced by rdf:type): `from rdflib import Graph, Node, URIRef`. Both `@prefix` lines (fhir:, rdf:) are used. Even so the notation ratio stays above 1 (1.018).
